articleTitle: Forest Fire Disaster Classification Using Artificial Neural Network Method
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: One of the leading causes of forest destruction is forest fires. In Indonesia, forest fires have caused forest damage to 354,582 hectares in 2022, or an increase of 19.4% from 296,942 hectares in 2020. This has caused enormous losses to the community’s economy, companies, and regional and state governments. One of the causes of forest fires caused by nature is the climate, where hot temperatures can cause the burning of dry branches or leaves, which eventually spread due to wind blowing and low rainfall. This study aims to classify forest fire data to categorize and predict forest fire disasters. The dataset used is the 2016 Algerian Forest Fire dataset, which was downloaded from the UC Repository with a total of 122 data on forest fires and labeled with categories, namely fire and non-fire. One classification method that is quite good at predicting data is Artificial Neural Network (ANN). The ANN method is highly accurate and adaptive to studying the training data. This study uses the ANN Backpropagation method in the classification process to obtain optimal results. Based on the classification results using the ANN Backpropagation method, optimal % accuracy results of 96% are obtained. At the same time, the model’s performance shows that the ANN Backpropagation method produces a recall value of 100%, precision of 91.66%, and f1-score of 95.65%. From the accuracy value generated in this study, this model can be a tool for predicting forest fire disasters before they occur. It can prevent and reduce forest damage.

articleTitle: Interactive Augmented Reality Implementation for Geomorphology by Using Open Data Source
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: The use of Augmented Reality (AR) technology has shown great potential in enhancing the learning experience in various fields, including geomorphological learning. Geomorphology studies the shape and process of formation of the earth’s surface. AR technology can be used as a learning aid to visualize and learn geomorphological concepts interactively. In the context of geomorphology, one can view and interact with 3D models of geomorphological forms such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coasts directly on a table or through a mobile device. The availability of free data, such as SRTM (Shuttle Radar Topographic Mission) and data from Google, allows the creation of 3D geomorphological models in all corners of the world. The ease of making this application is also supported by free software such as Blender, Unity Hub, and Vuforia Engine so that the creation of applications is more optimal. As a result, by using open-source data, AR applications are very easy and inexpensive to build. From this free and open data source software, 1 geomorphology application package was created in several unique locations from around the world (except the polar regions) to make geomorphology learning more enjoyable. For users, AR applications that have been built are quite easy to use. All respondents said that learning geomorphology with AR is more fun because it gives a real impression to the user.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Deep Neural Network based Gamelan Musical Instruments Separation
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: The use of Javanese gamelan instruments or playing idioms in gamelan is widely used in various film compositions, video games, and contemporary music. Most gamelan instruments are made of metal, so separating the signals between instruments in evaluating gamelan music compositions is challenging. The U-Net architecture is used to test various methods and features; therefore, it can be done to conduct a comparative study to find the best neural network methods and features for Music Source Separation (MSS) in Javanese gamelan music. The neural network method tested was selected from methods often used for sequential data, such as Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Dual Path Recurrent Neural Networks (DPRNN), and Hybrid Demucs. There are 2 spectrogram input representations tested in the network, namely the magnitude spectrogram with wiener filtering (WF) and complex-as-channels (CAC). On average, the Hybrid Demuc's Source-To-Distortion Ratio (SDR) has the best value of 7.9 dB. In tests carried out using the evaluation of Source-To-Distortion Ratio (SDR), Source-to-Artifact Ratio (SAR), and Source-to-Interference Ratio (SIR), it is known that DPRNN is 31% superior using complex-as-channels (CAC) compared to WF. In comparison, LSTM is 20% superior using CAC compared to WF.

articleTitle: Detecting Fake Reviews Using N-gram Model and Chi-Square
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Online product reviews are increasingly important in consumer purchasing decisions. They tend to refer to product or service reviews online before purchasing. Therefore, conducting more in-depth research in detecting fake reviews is essential. This research utilizes the n-gram model, especially bigrams and trigrams. The results of these two n-gram models were selected using the chi-square method. Next, the selected feature results are applied in three machine learning algorithms: Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, and Logistic Regression. SVM and Logistic Regression algorithms are suitable for use in binary classification, while Random Forest has the advantage of dealing with variations in the language and writing style of fake reviews. The best results in this research were obtained using the Support Vector Machine algorithm combined with trigrams and the chi-square method, with a value of K=1000. These results achieved an accuracy level of 92.19%. This achievement far exceeds previous research, which only achieved an accuracy of 88.75%. These results show that the approach of using word context and careful feature selection in detecting fake reviews improved the previous accuracy by 3.49%, even with the same algorithm.

articleTitle: Denoising Autoencoder-based Feature Compression for Enhanced Performance of Vehicle License Plate Image Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: To combat the issue of low-quality license plate images captured by CCTV cameras in Electronic Traffic Law Enforcement (ETLE) systems, this study presents a Denoising Autoencoder-based feature compression method for improved image recognition. The Denoising Autoencoder significantly outperforms the conventional Autoencoder, enhancing feature extraction by introducing noise to the input. The method increases the accuracy rate from the standalone use of a Convolutional Neural Network $(90.47 \%$) to $94.76 \%$, showcasing its effectiveness in noise reduction, dimensionality reduction, and feature learning from license plate images.

articleTitle: Revenge Pornography Matching Using Computer Vision
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: This paper examines the use of artificial intelligence (AI), multiple detection techniques, and image analysis methodologies while understanding the various specifics that must be taken into account for greater accuracy in order to develop an end-to-end solution to combat the proliferation of revenge and illegal pornographic material. The Ministry of Home Affairs approved the “Cyber Crime Prevention against Women and Children (CCPWC)” program, which enables the public to file complaints about child pornography/child sexual abuse material, rape/gang rape images, or sexually explicit material. Hence the goal of the project is to speed up the process of helping any victim of online harassment by using AI-ML, computer vision automation, and research to identify the source of any unauthorized digital content.

articleTitle: Identifying Facial and Body Movement Through CNN And Monocular Tracking Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Facial Expression movement could analyze the true meaning behind the person's intention, but people could lie and fabricate their real expression by restraining the facial muscle. However, multitasking and restraining, both facial and body movement could reveal their true intention. Facial and body movement studies have been conducted to study the true meaning behind someone's movement. Through these studies, we will subtract a few methods that are accurate to the true result through the testing that have been conducted. We proposed the utilization of Seetaface method and a hybrid of deep learning approach with inertial sensors to analyze human true emotions. Through the Seetaface method, we will analyze the person's facial movement, which consists of the important facial features such as eyes, nose and mouth. Subsequently, the hybrid of deep data and facial features will detect and analyze a person's body movement through a camera and record it to the body models data. After successfully processing both of the methods, our findings show that facial detection is capable of pointing to the facial feature and expression of important features, however hindered by face shifting and obstruction. In body detection, the true action matched 100% successfully with the prediction of the action result after further evaluation using hybrid best results.

articleTitle: Exploring the Accuracy of Artificial Intelligence in Detecting Lies Through Micro-expression Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Micro-expressions are the subtle and rapid movements of human facial expressions that could reveal a person’s true emotions, including emotions that people attempt to suppress, hide, or restrain. Many recent papers have researched facial expression recognition systems in video sequences using GRU models. However, they haven’t found a good relevance of micro-expression (ME) in detecting deceptive behaviors. In order to improve and contribute to the development of the system, we propose a micro-expression lie detection system with GRU’s hyperparameter optimization and explore its accuracy. FER-2013 is used for expression recognition learning and the dataset containing video clips of courtroom trials is used for deception detection learning. Several normalization techniques are done in the process. The CNN model with eight convolutional layers and three fully linked layers is used to train the facial expression recognition system. To improve its accuracy, multiple GRU parameter settings are employed. We used the model on the test dataset after training it. The outcome shows that it was 92.31% accurate. The confusion matrix predicts 12 out of 13 outcomes, with 100% accuracy on the deceptive class and 85% accuracy on the truthful class.

articleTitle: Answering Why-Not Questions on Range-Based Skyline Queries for Incomplete Data in Road Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Currently, knowledge and technology in data engineering are advancing rapidly. One area of development is data retrieval techniques with specific queries. Data that does not appear in certain query results raises the question of "why not?" Answering this question can be used to evaluate why the data does not appear in a particular search query.The why-not question can also be applied to range-based skyline queries. Skyline queries aim to find "interesting" data from any multidimensional data, e.g. set of spatial data with coordinates that can be mapped onto a Cartesian plane. In this case, the data being analyzed is road network data. However, not all acquired data has complete attributes. Sometimes, due to errors, certain attributes of the data are not recorded. Data that does not have a value for all attributes is referred to as incomplete data. This article aims to address the why-not problem in range-based skyline queries for incomplete road network data. Two strategies are used to answer this question: modifying attributes other than point coordinates and adjusting the maximum query distance. The computational algorithms compared are the local skyline approach and the naive one. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm performs better than the naive approach in terms of execution time.

articleTitle: Basketball Arm Shooting Robot Design by Implementing Parabolic Motion
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Not a few of the existing robotics technologies make robots with movements that are increasingly human-like. One of them is in the field of sports, namely basketball. In a basketball game, a parabolic motion will be seen when throwing the ball. However, it is difficult to see a real parabolic motion when it is carried out at a certain distance. With this research, it is expected to show a design of a basketball arm shooting robot by implementing parabolic motion. This system will be built by utilizing the angular velocity calculation method when throwing the ball. The component that will be used is the Arduino Uno microcontroller as the central controller that will control the movement. This microcontroller will be connected with 3 servos as actuators, XL4015 step-down module, and a capacitor. The result of this study is to design a basketball arm shooting robot by implementing parabolic motion using the Arduino IDE. Through this research, it is possible to find out the best throwing distance, which is a distance of 90 to 160 cm.

articleTitle: Utilization of Body Posture Feature Extraction with Movenet for Silat Movement Classification Using Artificial Neural Network (ANN)
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Pencak Silat is a distinctive traditional martial art of Indonesia that needs to be preserved. One way to preserve Pencak Silat through a technological approach is by introducing its movements using Human Pose Estimation. Human Pose Estimation is a branch of computer vision that predicts the position of keypoints on a human body from an image, in this case, images of Pencak Silat movements. One of the models for extracting keypoints is MoveNet, developed by Google, excelling in striking a balance between speed and precision. This study proposes a classification system for Pencak Silat movements using the Artificial Neural Network (ANN) architecture. It utilizes a dataset of Pencak Silat movements with keypoints extracted using MoveNet. The dataset includes 8 movements: ‘dengkulan’, ‘pukulan lurus’, ‘pukulan samping’, ‘sikap pasang’, ‘sikutan atas’, ‘sikutan depan’, ‘tendangan A’, and ‘tendangan T’. The research employs K-Fold Cross Validation with K=5 for validation. The research results demonstrate that by utilizing the body posture feature extraction with MoveNet, it is possible to classify Pencak Silat movements using the Artificial Neural Network (ANN) method, achieving an accuracy of 0.971, which indicates a good performance.

articleTitle: Digital Watermarking using Unsigned Integer for Image Authentication
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Active tampering detection systems based on watermarking are developing rapidly. This is in line with the increasing number of image manipulation processes that even ordinary people can easily use through various applications that can be used free of charge. The singular value-based watermarking method is very popular because of its good authentication capabilities but requires large computational costs. Several alternative solutions based on signed integer matrices such as Hadamard and Walsh are able to speed up the computational process and produce a good level of imperceptibility. The two matrices have the same characteristics in the first row and column, while the other ones have opposite integer signs. This study proposes the formation of a new matrix based on the characteristics of the Hadamard and Walsh matrix where the unused integer sign values will be removed. The test results show that all methods used have the same level of imperceptibility. In terms of embedding time, the Hadamard and Walsh-based method reduced the average time by 9% and 16% respectively compared to the singular value-based method, while the proposed method was able to achieve 20%. Similar results were also obtained during authentication where the Hadamard and Walsh method increased the speed by 9% and 18% while the proposed method was able to reach 20%. The proposed method is able to achieve the highest speed while maintaining the level of imperceptibility.

articleTitle: Predictive Analysis of Monthly Flood Variables in the Palangkaraya Area Using Multiple Regression Methods and MLR, NN, KNN, Random Forest, SVM Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Indonesia is a tropical area; weather forecasting is a challenge. Weather can be affected by temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, and precipitation. The multiple linear regression approach can predict rainfall precipitation. Rainfall is the dependent variable in this study, with temperature, humidity, irradiance, and wind speed as independent factors. The January to June 2023 dataset shows a minimum pressure value of 23.3 nPa on January 20, 2023, a minimum temperature value of 32 C on January 20, 2023, and a maximum pressure value of 25.3 nPa on May 20, 2023. 38.8 mm of rain fell on the ground on April 20, 2023.

articleTitle: The Impact of Text Preprocessing on Personality Analysis on Twitter Social Media Posts in Bahasa Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Many studies have addressed preprocessing, however none have explored the impact of various preprocessing techniques or determined the optimal combination for personality analysis. Therefore, this research focuses on implementing various preprocessing techniques to identify which combination yields the best prformance in personality analysis. The preprocessing process involves normalization, cleaning, stopword removal, and stemming. Additionally, this study incorporates feature extraction using N-Gram features, including unigram, bigram, and trigram. Based on the results of several testing scenarios, the best system performance was achieved using the combination of preprocessing techniques: case folding + normalization + cleaning + stemming, resulting in an accuracy of 79%. Furthermore testing with the application of unigram feature extraction yielded better accuracy compared to bigram and trigram. Normalization plays a significant role in preprocessing, as words on Twitter often use non-standard language, and the purpose of normalization is to transform non-standard words into standard ones.

articleTitle: Automatic License Plate Recognition System in Indonesia Using YOLOv8 and EasyOCR Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: In this era of ever-evolving technology, people are in great demand for a safe and secure lifestyle and travel. The number of motorized vehicles on the road has steadily increased over the past decade. However, this also brings negative impacts such as congestion, air pollution, and decreased safety. Therefore, an effective automatic vehicle license plate detection and recognition system is needed to improve traffic safety and surveillance. This research develops an automated vehicle license plate detection system with the You Only Look Once (YOLO) algorithm. The dataset in this study uses images of vehicles and Indonesian license plates totaling 869 data. Then, proceed with the text extraction process on the vehicle license plate using the Easy Optical Character Recognition (EasyOCR) library. The test results to develop an automatic vehicle license plate detection system with the YOLOv8 algorithm and the EasyOCR library have an accuracy rate of 94%. These results show that the system has successfully detected and recognized all characters on the vehicle license plate.

articleTitle: Real-time Fall Detection using Key Joint Position Transition Time in the Elderly Activity Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: The aging population is rapidly increasing worldwide, leading to a growing concern for the well-being of elderly individuals. Falls among the elderly pose a significant threat to their health and independence, often resulting in serious injuries and reduced quality of life. To address this issue, accurate fall estimation methods are essential for timely intervention and effective preventive measures. By combining wearable sensors and machine learning algorithms can develop robust and reliable fall detection and prediction systems. However, it’s important to acknowledge that wearable sensors can come with certain drawbacks, primarily related to their cost, installation, and convenience. Compared to some high-end wearable sensor systems, setting up video cameras can be more affordable. Therefore, we propose a novel system for fall detection utilizing pose estimation framework (PoseNet) on the real-time camera. PoseNet detects the pose and estimates its key-joint position, the falling position or not using are classified using the time difference between the start and end of the pose change. K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) is used as classifier. From the test, the resulting accuracy, precision, recall, and F-1 scores were 95%, 90%, 100%, and 93.23%, respectively. By providing a comprehensive monitoring solution, the proposed system enhances the safety and well-being of elderly individuals. Its ability to not only detect falls but also monitor daily activities and respond to emergencies immediately makes it a valuable tool for improving the quality of care and support for the elderly population.

articleTitle: Segmentation of White Blood Cells in M1, M2, and M3 Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) Images Using Deep Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Leukemia is a cancer of the spinal cord and blood. A haematology analyzer diagnoses leukemia based on manual counting of white blood cells (WBCs) so it takes a lot of time and costs. Several methods with mathematical basis have been developed for detecting undeveloped cells so that can provide good performance for the segmentation. This research aims to segment WBCs on M1, M2, and M3 Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) images and test the performance results of segmentation using the Deep Convolutional Neural Network (Deep CNN) with previous studies used Active Contour without Edge (ACWE) and Watershed Distance Transform (WDT) for segmentation. The Deep CNN used was DeepLab v3+ with pretrained ResNet-50. M1, M2, and M3 AML images were taken from the Dr. Sardjito Hospital laboratory in Yogyakarta. The Fiji application was used to create ground truth mask images from the original data as a true label so they could be trained in the DeepLab v3+ model with pretrained ResNet-50 in 5-fold proportions of data with K-Fold Cross Validation and used the different number of filters. The results of the training model were used for new data segmentation of M1, M2, and M3 AML images. The highest average accuracy and average mIoU 5-fold cross-validation results between filters 64, 128, and 256 were obtained by the number of filters 256 of 0.9101 (91.01%) and 0.9060 (90.60%). This result surpassed previous research which used ACWE and WDT methods with an increase of 0.0722 (7.22%) for the number of filters 256.

articleTitle: Comparing the Efficiency of State-Feedback Controllers in Stabilizing Two-Wheeled Robot
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: A two-wheeled robot is an intriguing example of a self-balancing robot that captivates the interest of many hobbyists and engineers. Due to its inherent nature, the mechanical structure alone can not achieve stability, necessitating the use of an appropriate controller. In this paper, we are comparing state-feedback controllers based on two methods: the Coefficient Diagram Method (CDM) and the Linear-Quadratic Regulator (LQR), with the goal of stabilizing the two-wheeled robot. The simulation results confirm that both controllers are capable of quickly stabilizing the pitching angle of the two-wheeled robot. Here, the LQR-based controller exhibits slightly faster responses compared to the CDM-based controller. The settling times are 0.1555 seconds and 0.1211 seconds, consecutively for CDM and LQR. It can be said that the difference is not significant. Despite the slower response time, the CDM-based controller proves to be more efficient in terms of control effort when compared to LQR. The results show that the CDM-based controller requires only 61 percent control effort used by the LQR-based controller for stabilizing the two-wheeled robot.

articleTitle: Breast Cancer Detection on Mammographic Image using Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Breast cancer had led the prevalence cancer cases in Indonesia and it had become the fourth leading cause of death worldwide in 2020. The risk can be minimized by regularly conducting early screenings. This study implements the Deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) method to build an artificial intelligence model for early detection of breast cancer on mammography images. Using 2400 training data in total and 120 test data for testing which each contains 50% normal and cancer images. The proposed CNN Architecture has 3 layers which implement average and max pooling layer. The training reach 100% of maximum training accuracy and 91.67% of maximum validation accuracy. The selected model is used to classify new unseen dana and it produces 60.83% accuracy which achieved by using optimizer adam, 0.001 learning rate, and 10 epochs. The result was obtained after several parameter training using epoch, learning rate, layers, optimizer, and adjustment to the dataset.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis in Product Reviews with Maximum Entropy and Naïve Bayes Using N-gram Method
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Online shoppers now primarily rely on product reviews and user experiences shared on social media platforms before making an online purchase. The opportunity to capture product sentiments on social media has drawn interest in data mining analysis as it provides exciting ideas to support business growth and success. The two biggest online retailers, Amazon and Shein product reviews will be analyzed with the Maximum Entropy and Naive Bayes using the n-grams approach based on precision, recall, f-1 score, and accuracy. This study will also evaluate their time complexities depending on hardware and software requirements. Findings reveal that Maximum Entropy with n-grams generated improved accuracy performance, particularly with unigram, with an average accuracy rating of 91.5% compared to Naive Bayes with n-grams. However, the Naïve Bayes performs better when tested on different hardware and software specifications. Thus, the Naive Bayes algorithm performs better in execution time, and the Maximum Entropy using the n-gram approach resulted in improved accuracy.

articleTitle: Analysis of Factors in TikTok Shopping Cart and Live Streaming that Affect TikTok Application User Satisfaction
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: This research is intended to determine the factors in TikTok’s shopping cart and live streaming features that can satisfy their users, such as represent, talent communication, Functionality, context, Reliability, and system integration. The research model used is the Delone & McLean and SEM SmartPLS software as an analysis tool. The number of samples obtained was 404 respondents with a calculation formula using Slovin. The research technique used is non-probability with snowball sampling type. Based on the results of the analysis carried out, the represent factor (4.867), talent communication factor (3.733), and functionality factor (7.455) have a significant influence. In contrast, the context factor (1.658), reliability factor (0.896), and system integration factor (0.274) do not have a significant influence on the satisfaction of the TikTok application users.

articleTitle: Multi-Class Classification of Skin Diseases Using ResNet50
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: The World Health Organization (WHO) reports that cancer is one of the leading causes of death globally and is responsible for approximately 10 million deaths yearly. Globally, about 1 in 6 deaths are attributed to cancer. As the body’s outermost organ, the skin is vulnerable to various diseases, and accurate diagnosis is crucial for effective treatment. However, limited access to dermatologists and expensive skin biopsies pose challenges to efficient diagnosis. In this research, we utilized the ResNet50 model to classify seven types of skin diseases. We employed the HAM10000 dataset, which consists of images representing disease classes such as akiec, bbc, bkl, df, mel, vasc, and nv. The ResNet50 model was trained and evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1score performance metrics. The research findings reveal that the ResNet50 model achieved a high level of accuracy, with an accuracy rate of 91.71% on the test data. The precision, recall, and F1-Score metrics also demonstrated excellent performance, with 91.89%, 92.04%, and 91.87% respectively. These results confirm the model’s effectiveness in classifying various skin diseases, demonstrating high precision for accurate identification and high recall for locating all actual instances. The balanced F1-Score emphasizes the model’s proficiency in diagnosis, advancing skin disease classification with ResNet50. Overall, these findings contribute to advancing skin disease diagnosis using the ResNet50 model and highlight its efficacy in achieving accurate and reliable classification results.

articleTitle: Comparison Analysis of Plastic Optical Fiber as a Replacement for Copper Cables for Car Communication Links
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Car Copper cables are recognized for their high interference performance, resulting in increased vehicle weight and slower transition speeds. This paper examines the feasibility of employing multimode plastic optical fiber technology as a better solution to traditional copper cables in-car communication systems, specifically focusing on the Tesla Model Y. The study thoroughly investigates the car’s fiber optic cable system, emphasizing weight reduction, cost estimation, power link budget, rise time budget, and transmission speed. The research demonstrates significant potential for weight reduction by replacing copper cables with Plastic Optical Fiber (POF), achieving a remarkable saving of 61.47% in total cable weight. The Power link budget analysis confirmed feasibility with a total power loss of around 14 dB and received power of around −16 dB when utilized with a −2 dBm transmitter. Rise time budget analysis confirms feasibility, with most links showing a rise time of around 0.5 ns—0.2 ns faster than the system maximum. The unique light characteristic of optical fiber contributes to overall vehicle weight reduction, improved speed and capacity, enhanced security and stability, and increased energy efficiency.

articleTitle: Development of a Data Transmission Security System on a Mobile Smart Trash Bin Using an Elliptic Curve Cryptography Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: The Internet of Things requires data transmission to exchange information, transmit data, and carry out various functions. However, data transmission involving these communication protocols is still vulnerable to attack. One of the protocols that is still vulnerable to attacks is the Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) protocol. This protocol is vulnerable to Man In The Middle (MITM) attacks which attack packet data that will be sent between the device and the server. Therefore, a method of securing data transmission is needed on the Internet of Things system. This research creates a data transmission security system for Mobile Smart Trash Bin device communication using a Virtual Private Network (VPN) secured by Transport Layer Security (TLS) using an asymmetric Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC) algorithm. The system is tested by testing functionality, security, performance, and Quality of Service. From the test results, it is known that the system functionality has been running according to design; it can encrypt data communication between the robot and the server; has better throughput, average time, and error rate than without using a VPN; and get the results of a throughput value of 3048 bits/sec, a delay value of 381 ms, a jitter of 381 ms, and 0% packet loss.

articleTitle: The Impact of Data Augmentation on Prototypical Networks for Open-Set Face Identification
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Extensive research has been conducted on face recognition for large training datasets, and it continues to be an active study area. The present study aimed to examine the issue of open-set face recognition using the ITB Frontal Profile Limited Dataset (IFPLD). This dataset comprises a single frontal and profile face image for each subject. The system is trained to determine, given a profile face of an individual, which frontal face pertains to the same individual. As a result of the constrained dataset accessible for training and testing purposes, the face identification problem is considered a few-shot-open-set problem. Prototypical networks are applicable for face recognition on the IFPLD because they are one of the meta-learning techniques used to address the few-shot learning problem. This study investigates the effect of adding data augmentation to training and testing Prototypical Network on the IFPLD dataset by proposing two distinct techniques for identifying a query profile face. Our investigation using the standard model for few-shot learning (FSL) shows that method 2 achieved higher accuracy, 86.2% for 5-ways-1-shot and 66.3% accuracy for 20-ways-1-shot scenarios.

articleTitle: Type-2 Fuzzy Sliding Mode Control Design for Self-Balancing Mobile Robot
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Mobile robots have been a popular research topic in recent decades due to their many potential applications. One of the common types of mobile robots is the two-wheeled self-balancing robot, which operates based on the basic concept of an inverted pendulum. This concept represents an unstable system, so a proper controller is required to stabilize the system. This paper proposes a controller that combines a type2 fuzzy logic system and sliding mode control to stabilize and maintain the robot’s body balance in a straight upright position. Sliding mode control is a well-known robust controller with the ability to handle system disturbances. However, the presence of a switching law in sliding mode control can lead to the occurrence of chattering phenomena. Hence, a type-2 fuzzy logic system is applied to reduce the chattering effect by adjusting the switching gain of the sliding mode control. Additionally, the system’s stability is analyzed using the Lyapunov theorem. The simulation results demonstrate that the designed type-2 fuzzy sliding mode control not only reduces chattering but also decreases energy consumption by approximately 59.92% and reduces the undershoot of the pitching rate by about 33.5%, with only a 0.115-second longer settling time for pitching angle compared to conventional sliding mode control.

articleTitle: A Modified Artificial Potential Field using Perpendicular Force for Leader-Follower System
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Artificial potential field (APF) is a path planning strategy that is widely used in robotics. Unfortunately, it is susceptible to local minima problems, especially on Symmetrically Aligned Robot-Obstacle-Goal (SAROG) configurations. In this paper, we propose a modified APF by introducing the perpendicular force for escaping the local minima. Furthermore, it is also being implemented for the leader-follower system. Here, the leader is assigned to reach the goal while avoiding obstacles. Simultaneously, the follower needs to track the leader while maintaining a safe distance. The effectiveness of our proposed method is verified by numerical simulations. The results show that the modified APF using perpendicular prevails in guiding the leader to reach the goal. At the same time, the follower can maintain a tolerated distance from the leader.

articleTitle: Hyperparameter Optimalization on Transfer Learning Method to Classify Mango Varieties
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Mango is a garden plant that comes from Asia and has many varieties. Mango fruit varieties can be identified through the characteristics of fruit shape, fruit color, and leaf texture. However, these characteristics have the same tendency so it is difficult to distinguish for some people. This research aims to classify mango fruit variety that implement convolutional neural networks method with transfer learning using DenseNet201, InceptionResNetV2 and Xception architecture. The datasets consist of 1600 images divided by 8 classes. To get the highest accuracy, Experiments were carried out on different transfer learning architectures, input shape, optimizer algorithms, and learning rate values. The result of this study is a machine learning model with 100% testing accuracy obtained through the use of DenseNet201 architecture, Adam optimizer and 0.0001 learning rate value.

articleTitle: Interpretation and Performance Machine Learning Model for Detection of Brain Stroke Based on Classifier
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Several diseases, such as Brain Stroke, are one of the causes of death, one that can be utilized in disease detection, especially Brain Stroke, is Machine Learning (ML), several models that can be used in predicting the likelihood of a patient having a brain stroke are one of them; Logistic Regression, SVM, XGBoost, Naïve Bayes, Extra Tree, CatBoost Classification, LightGBM, Random Forest, Decision Tree, Gradient Boosting, k-NN. Some studies are still little using model interpretation and Model Performance using Mean Cross-Validation Scores. The Study aims to examine the accuracy-based classification performance of various ML models and interpret the model using SelectKBest to fill this little research gap. The results show that CatBoost has the best accuracy of 94.3% and SVM best model performance with Score (Mean-Cross Validation Score) of 0.951, and the "hypertension" and "heart_disease" features are the most influential features based on the K Score (SelectKBest), where the results are "72,928" and "74,706".

articleTitle: Forecasting the effect of parameters on AQI values with Machine learning: Multiple Linear Regression
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: This study analyzes the Air Quality Index (AQI) in Yogyakarta. The results of AQI in Yogyakarta show significant fluctuations. The main causes of air quality changes are human activities, including transportation, industry, and biomass burning. In addition, the influence of weather and topography of the region also contribute to the variation of $A Q I$. In addition, the influence of weather and regional topography also contribute to the variation of $A Q I$. The finding that human activities, including transportation and industry, contribute significantly to air quality fluctuations indicates that mitigation measures need to be taken immediately to maintain healthy air quality in Yogyakarta. This study uses a multiple linear regression method to predict the Air Quality Index (AQI). The data used includes AQI measurements, rainfall, humidity, wind speed, and concentrations of air pollutants such as PM2.5, PM10, and SO2 concentrations. Because the multiple linear regression method accommodates nonlinear relationships, variable interpretation, correlation measurement, and fast prediction and is easy to implement. The results showed that the best scenario was in scenario 2 with an accuracy of $99.96 \%$, and the lowest result was obtained in scenario 3 with an accuracy of $33.77 \%$. The X variables that have the greatest influence on the AQI Index Value include Pm 2.5, Pm 10, So2 and Weather with a proximity value $\geq 50: 1$, and X variables that have no effect include Events and Wind with a proximity value < 50:1.

articleTitle: Performance and Accuracy Analysis of the ResNet50 Transfer Learning Model for Melanoma Cancer Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: An important component in the treatment of severe skin diseases is the early diagnosis of melanoma cancer. To assess the effectiveness and accuracy of the model, this paper analyzes the classification of melanoma cancer using the ResNet50 model. ResNet-50 increases the possibility of detecting melanoma cancer at an early stage with the combination of its strong feature extraction capabilities and deep structure. It also increases the chances of successful treatment and a better prognosis. In the dataset of photos labeled “benign“ and “malignant”, augmentation techniques such as rotation, zoom, vertical inversion, and horizontal inversion are used to improve model performance. The results showed that the model with a calculation time of one hour and forty-five minutes achieved $86 \%$ accuracy. By utilizing this augmentation strategy, the model’s capacity to identify melanoma cancer cases has been enhanced, thereby making a significant contribution to the field of cancer detection research. This study offers a new perspective on the use of the ResNet50 model for melanoma cancer classification and raises the possibility of using related approaches to address other health problems.

articleTitle: Measuring Meaning Similarity Using TF/IDF and Term Synonym ID
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: This work proposes a novel alternative for measuring the meaning similarity between two sentences in Bahasa Indonesia. Two sentences are considered to have the same meaning if each word in those sentences has the same synonym. In this regard, a synonym database is needed. In this study, the synonym database was developed by categorizing words with the same meaning. Each word group was given a unique ID. The first scenario was performed without stemming, while the second was performed with stemming during the pre-processing. Each word in the sentence was matched to the synonym database using the synonym ID reference. The synonym ID was weighed using TF/IDF, and the vector distance was measured using Cosine similarity. The most optimal test result was noticed in the first scenario with a 89.72% similarity score out of 80 data tests, higher than the second scenario with an 76.24% similarity score.

articleTitle: Implementation of Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Units for Text Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Although text contains a wealth of information, it can be challenging and time-consuming because it is unstructured. Text categorization can be utilized to organize, arrange, and categorize nearly anything. Knowing how bidirectional GRU functions, this research was done to categorize data using that model. Information can cycle through this network for a very long time because of the use of recurrent connections in the depicted standard Bi GRU design. This study uses a dataset of 20 newsgroups and over 18,000 newsgroup documents obtained from The UCI KDD Archive. Bidirectional GRU is also used to classify it. Bidirectional GRU can remove cell states and transfer information utilizing concealed states. The reset gate and update gate are two of the GRU's gates. Each gate has its weight and bias because the gates are neural networks. A validation accuracy value of 0.8456 and an accuracy value of 0.9965 were obtained from an experiment including ten epochs. A validation loss value of 0.7144 and a loss value of 0.0144 were also discovered. This is a successful classification of text using deep learning algorithms.

articleTitle: Rice Disease Image Classification using MobileNetV2 Pretrained Model with Attention Visualization using Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM)
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Rice is one of the staple foods in Asia, particularly in Indonesia. With an ever-increasing demand of food, a stable rice production is mandatory and pest is one of the major challenges faced in sustainable rice production. In this research, we proposed an image classification model based on the MobileNetV2 pretrained model combined with a visual explanation based on the gradient-weighted class activation (Grad-CAM) algorithm to build a robust and accurate classification of rice diseases. The model is based on convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture. First, transfer learning is done from the MobileNetV2 pretrained model to create the classification model, followed by Grad-CAM to produce the visual explanation of the CNN. Finally, the model is trained on 7,077 rice images containing four different diseases (bacterial blight, blast, brown spot, and tungro) with a data augmentation process to increase the dataset’s overall variance. This process yields a model with a classification accuracy of up to 99,9%, combined with visual feature explanation making this model a robust and efficient classification model.

articleTitle: Towards Sustainable Energy Distribution: IoT-Based Monitoring of Electrical Load Parameters in a Hybrid Renewable Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: The transition towards sustainable energy sources has led to the rapid adoption of hybrid renewable power plants that integrate multiple energy generation technologies. However, the efficient distribution of energy from these diverse sources remains a challenge due to the complex nature of their operation. This paper proposes an approach for sustainable energy distribution by implementing IoT telemetry monitoring of electrical load parameters in a hybrid renewable power plant. The study focuses on leveraging wireless communication technology to monitor and optimize the electrical load parameters in realtime. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, a case study is conducted on a hybrid renewable power plant and shows a low error percentage and high accuracy.

articleTitle: A Multi-scalar SPEI Drought Index Prediction Using Long Short-Term Memory
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: The Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) is a type of drought index that can be used to analyze the level of drought in a study area. This study aims to predict the SPEI drought index on a multi-time scale of 1,3, and 6 using the LSTM method. Testing was carried out with several trials on several datasets of 5 tests. The distribution of the SPEI index dataset consists of training and testing data in the order of 92/46,115/46,138/46,161/46, and 184 /64 for each of the SPEI-1, SPEI-3, and SPEI-6 indices. The results of tests that have been carried out on the SPEI multime scale show that the SPEI-6 index can provide the lowest RMSE value of 0.05 in the fifth scenario or with the 184/64 dataset modeling. This study shows that the LSTM method can reasonably predict drought levels for SPEI drought index data with a longer time scale and with an adequate number of datasets.

articleTitle: An Evaluation on the Wind Speed Forecasting Model Using the ARIMA and SARIMA Methods Based on the MSE Value
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Wind speed in archipelago areas has an impact on fishing activities, transportation, ocean currents and wave height, as well as maritime weather. An accurate information about wind speed is needed. Wind speed forecasting data within a certain time can be used for decision making in transportation as well as the development of renewable energy technologies. Wind speed is a type of time series data. The ARIMA and SARIMA, are methods of evaluating and analyzing time series data that are widely used in this era. This study uses the ARIMA and SARIMA methods to forecast daily wind speed data from October 2022 to March 2023. This data is the result of measurements from the Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) Hang Nadim Batam station. Model accuracy is an important factor when analyzing time series data. Therefore, the best ARIMA and SARIMA models will be determined based on the smallest MSE value. The four best models were obtained from the stages of the temporal model determination process by observing ACF and PACF graphic patterns, namely ARIMA(2,0,0), ARIMA(0,1,1), ARIMA(1,1,1) and SARIMA(1,1,0)(1,1,1)s. This study finding that the ARIMA (1,1,1) model is the best model with the smallest MSE value 6.72465.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Car Detection System Using Convolutional Neural Network and Haar Cascade Classifier
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Advances in technology have played an important role in increasing the efficiency of the transportation system in Indonesia. However, the rapid growth in private vehicles has also caused significant traffic congestion in many areas. An innovative solution is needed to manage traffic, and one of the proposed solutions is using a Smart Traffic Light System. This system utilizes the latest vehicle object detection technology to dynamically adjust the duration of traffic lights based on the number of vehicles detected in each lane. This study presents an approach using two vehicle detection methods: the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and the Haar Cascade Classifier. The average accuracy value generated by the system is 86%, but this method shows a very high level of precision, reaching 100%, which means there are almost no errors in detecting vehicles. The recall of this method also reaches 86%, indicating the ability to detect most of the vehicles passing through the traffic lane. The results of this study indicate a strong potential for implementing a vehicle detection system with a combination method of CNN and Haar Cascade Classifier to overcome traffic congestion problems. The use of sophisticated and intelligent detection technology in the Smart Traffic Light system is expected to increase traffic efficiency, reduce waiting times, and optimize road use. Thus, this research makes an essential contribution to the development of a transportation system that is more adaptive and responsive to dynamic traffic.

articleTitle: Study on Effect of Degradation of Time Synchronization in IEEE 802.1AS Caused by Congestion on QoS of TAS and CBS
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: This paper quantitatively evaluates the effect of the degradation of the time synchronization accuracy of IEEE 802.1AS, a protocol for time synchronization over Ethernet, on the QoS of an in-vehicle network with IEEE 802.1TSN(Time-Sensitive Networking) by experiment. In IEEE 802.1AS, slave terminals synchronize the time to a master terminal by receiving the current time of the clock of the master terminal by gPTP. However, since it takes some time to transmit the time information due to the network delay, adjusting the time gap between the slave terminal and the master terminal is required. Since the adjustment is performed according to the measurement of the delay between a slave terminal and a master terminal, it will be affected by network congestion where gPTP messages are transmitted. To study the degradation of the time synchronization accuracy caused by congestion of in-vehicle networks, the authors evaluate the QoS of TAS and CBS, one of the QoS controls of IEEE 802.1TSN, over congested experimental networks. The experimental results show that the maximum delay and the coefficient of variation of the delay degraded owing to the congestion for TAS. However, it also indicates that the QoS of CBS is not always affected by the degradation of the time synchronization caused by the congestion.

articleTitle: Analysis of factors influencing the use of the Online Learning Management System after Covid-19 with the D&M Model
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: This study aims to determine the factors significantly influencing student satisfaction using the Online Learning Management System (LMS), especially after the covid 19 pandemic. This research focuses on several variables: Course Content (CC), Course Content Support (CCS), Course Assessment (CA), Course Design (CD), Device Compatibility (DC), Device Connectivity (DCO), Assurance (A), and System Reliability (R). The sample was 421 respondents from university students and academics from Indonesia and abroad. The research model used is the D&M model with purposive sampling technique and processed with SEM-Smart Partial Least Square (SmartPLS) version 4. From the results of the analysis, it is found that Course Content (4,719), Course Assessment (2,935), Course Design (2,560), Device Connectivity (7,632), and Assurance $(2,955)$ are factors that provide satisfaction to the intended application users. At the same time, Course Content Support $(1,879)$, Device Compatibility $(0,389)$, and Reliability $(1,036)$ do not influence the intended application. The results of these findings will more or less help improve the management of an institution regarding how to properly organize online learning so that the quality of the implementing institution is maintained.

articleTitle: Diabetes Classification Problem with CatBoost Method and Optuna Gradient Boosting Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a dangerous global epidemic that can cause kidney failure, heart attack, blindness, and death. The main cause of this disease is too high blood sugar levels due to the irrelevant work of pancreatic beta cells. Rapid computer technology advances and implementations based on artificial intelligence have penetrated various fields, especially the health sector. Data mining and machine learning are technologies that continue to grow, are reliable, and can be used as research support tools in the medical field. This technology is considered capable of helping to automate diabetes prediction. Based on related research, our contribution to this research is to utilize the CatBoost method with Optuna optimization. In the data preprocessing stage, all 768 data sets have gone through removing outliers, normalizing features to reducing dimensions. The dataset is divided into $85 \%$ composition for training data and $15 \%$ for test data. At the feature selection stage with Correlation Pearson’s, we found that Glucose correlated with diabetes outcome or disease because it had a value range of 0.47. The results’ accuracy is considered less than optimal because it only produces an accuracy value below $80 \%$, even after optimization with Optuna. It can be seen that there was only an increase of $7 \%$ after optimizing with Optuna.

articleTitle: Evaluation Quality Of E-Learning X Using ISO/IEC 25010 Framework And Design Thinking Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Technological developments have entered the digital 5.0 era, all areas of life including the field of education are required to be digital-based so that they can remain competitive with their competitors in order to continue to grow and develop. The need for applications that can support formal and informal educational institutions in today’s digital era is urgently needed, for this reason it is necessary to build an application platform as a digital media space that can carry out teaching and learning processes anytime and anywhere, such as e-learning applications. However, this e-learning application still needs to be reviewed for quality in terms of user satisfaction. This study aims to provide a comprehensive evaluation framework, provide guidelines for educational institutions for e-learning applications, and select quality e-learning platforms. Data collection methods through interviews and questionnaires. By using the ISO/IEC 25010 standard to evaluate the quality of e-learning. As well as using a design thinking approach to evaluate interfaces and user interactions in e-learning. From the results of testing the reliability of the questionnaire points distributed. Based on testing of 8 questionnaires filled out by 204 respondents, an average Raw.r value of 0.9 was obtained so that it can be said that the 8 questionnaires tested were reliable. To find out whether the user is successful or not in running the application usage scenario, a metric is used in the form of a success rate with an average yield of 9.2%. The results of this research can also provide in-depth insight into the quality of e-learning, as well as identify areas that need improvement to improve user experience.

articleTitle: Caries Level Classification using Combination of Hu and Zernike Invariant Moments Features and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: One of the most important parts of the human body is the teeth. In the human body, teeth are used as a digestive process and a beauty in the human body. Thus, it is necessary to prevent dental disease so that the teeth can function properly. Dental caries is the most common dental disease in everyday life. With advances in technology, artificial intelligence systems or image processing can be used in the process of diagnosing dental caries images. A total of 4 classes of dental caries imagery were used in this study, namely classes 1, 2, 3, and 4. The dental caries image consisted of 347 which were divided into 314 training images and 33 test images. The purpose of this study is to design a computer-based dental caries level classification system with image processing that uses a combination of the Hu and Zernike Moment Invariant Method used for feature extraction and the Machine Learning Method (KNN) used for dental caries classification in the Matlab 2020a application. The results of the classification that has been carried out will obtain the KNN accuracy value. The highest accuracy is the KNN method with an accuracy of 94.07% when using the combination of Hu and Zernike Moment Invariant feature extraction algorithms.

articleTitle: Predict Wildfires in Kalimantan using MODIS Products with Linear Regression, Gradient Boosting and Decision Tree algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Wildfires in Kalimantan pose a serious threat to the environment and ecological sustainability. Previous research may have limitations in addressing common problems associated with forest fire prediction such as uncertainties in weather data and other factors that may affect forest fires, so in an attempt to address these issues, this research focuses on using MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) products and applying linear regression, Gradient Boosting Regressor (GBR), and Decision Tree Regressor (DTR) algorithms to predict forest fires in Kalimantan. Data collected by MODIS, such as surface temperature, thermal anomalies, and other environmental variables, are used as inputs for the prediction model. Linear regression algorithms were used to analyze the relationship between these variables and develop a forest fire prediction model. The results showed that both models, GBR obtained a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) value of 9.76 with an accuracy value of 91.36% while DTR obtained an RMSE value of 9.85 with an accuracy value of 91.21%, which both models have high accuracy with a good level of variability explanation, indicated by R2 score close to 1.0. and therefore the GBR model may be preferred as a forest fire prediction model in Kalimantan based on the evaluation results obtained.

articleTitle: Layout Analysis for Robust Resume Parsing
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Document layout analysis is an important step in extracting information from documents of various structures. Layout data helps to understand the hierarchical structure of the document and create structured information for further analysis. Therefore, it has advantages in document parsing or semantic segmentation compared to CNN or transformer-based detection methods, or sentence classification approaches. In the human resources domain, most processes could also benefit from document intelligence. For instance, automated resume parsing is a key step for further analysis of these documents to use with tasks like candidate screening, matching, and could also benefit from document layout analysis methods. In this study, it is assumed that the specific layout structure of a resume document could help to resolve hierarchical information that is useful for detecting particular segments like education, experiments, skills, etc. From this point, it is aimed to explore the contribution of layout analysis to resume parsing in this paper. State-of-the-art methods that performed well in public document datasets are compared in terms of accuracy on hierarchical structure estimation of resume PDF documents. Additionally, a resume layout analysis model trained using custom layout categories. A custom-built data set was used for the training and evaluation of the proposed method. It is shown that fine-tuning with a small set of data improves the accuracy of general-purpose layout detection models on more specific tasks.

articleTitle: Supervised STDP Learning with Weight Decay for Spiking Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: This research aims to address the challenges of the Diehl & Cook model and develop a new learning method focused on the learning efficiency of spiking neural networks (SNNs). The identified challenges include the task of classification, learning redundancy, and catastrophic forgetting. To overcome these challenges, a novel approach called supervised STDP learning was proposed, leveraging the local learning nature of the STDP learning rule. Additionally, a weight decay mechanism was introduced to assign inhibitory roles to irrelevant weights. Experimental evaluations were conducted using the MNIST dataset, comparing the proposed method with the Diehl & Cook model. The results demonstrated that the proposed method significantly improved accuracy compared to the previous model, and the learning convergence speed was remarkably fast. The experiments also confirmed that supervised STDP learning allows for local learning within synapses, enabling the network to learn independently for each label without interference. As a result, the proposed method showed immunity to catastrophic forgetting. Overall, this research contributes to enhancing the learning efficiency of SNNs and provides insights into overcoming challenges in spiking neural network models.

articleTitle: Augmented Reality in Mobile Apps for Fashion Industry: A Quality Assessment based on ISO 25010
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Advanced technological developments and innovations are one of the significant factors of enhancing any industry to become more effective and efficient. Augmented Reality (AR) has arisen as a popular advanced technology as it provides a unique experience for various stakeholders. The fashion industry is no exception for AR technology. However, the quality of AR feature in mobile application is crucial for ensuring consumer satisfaction. To evaluate the quality of AR feature in mobile application, this journal presents the results of testing AR feature on mobile application in the fashion industry, in reference to model for quality according to ISO/IEC 25010. The evaluation will be tested in the aspects of performance efficiency, reliability, portability, functional suitability, and usability. The result of this research is to indicate which aspect from ISO 25010 that needs to be considered for improving the quality of AR feature in mobile application to achieve greater customer satisfaction of AR technology.

articleTitle: Transfer Learning and Fine-tuning Effect Analysis on Classification of Cat Breeds using a Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Cats are the most popular pets because they are adorable, entertaining, and can be used as companions when lonely. Its attractive appearance is one of the most popular animals in the world. However, various cat breeds in the world have different physical characteristics. To find out the type of cat breed, you can do a Deoxyribonucleic Acid (DNA) test. Unfortunately, DNA testing is costly and takes a long time. With Artificial Intelligence technology, a system is needed to classify cat breeds, namely the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). This research aims to analyze the effect of transfer learning and fine-tuning on the classification of cat breeds using CNN. This research used a dataset from Oxford-IIIT Pet, which consisted of 12 classes, namely Abyssinian, Bengal Birman, Bombay, British Shorthair, Egyptian Mau, Maine Coon, Persian, Ragdoll, Russian Blue, Siamese, and Sphynx with a total of 2,400 images. This research uses parameters with an architecture using Xception and RMSprop optimization with a learning rate 0.0001. This research has two scenarios: CNN with transfer learning and CNN with transfer learning and fine-tuning. This research achieved 92.5% accuracy on CNN with transfer learning and fine-tuning.

articleTitle: Mall Customer Clustering Using Gaussian Mixture Model, K-Means, and BIRCH Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Nowadays, online shopping has become the norm of customers around the world, therefore businesses need ways to identify their customer demographics, one of the way available is by using machine learning clustering algorithms to help in clustering customer demographic. This research paper aims to study machine learning algorithms which can be used to cluster customers based on the features which define them, those being: Gender, Age, Annual Income, Spending Score (1-100). The study employs clustering algorithms such as GMM (Gaussian Mixture Model), K-Means Clustering, and BIRCH. The metric Davies Bouldin Score is used to measure the quality of clusters produced by these 3 different algorithms. The findings show that K-Means clustering is the best clustering algorithm to be used in clustering the customers because in this case, the dataset which was used is more suitable to be clustered in this algorithm, however the other algorithms also perform good when the dataset suits them, overall, the findings can be used to better understand the business’ customer demographic. The implications of this study extend to various sectors of marketing, including e-commerce, retail, digital marketing, where marketing strategies are employed to gain a competitive edge.

articleTitle: Towards Improved Age Verification System for Security in Social Media using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with ResNet-50
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Social media is an excellent platform to communicate with loved ones, friends, discover new information, and more. Social media is used by many different kinds of people which makes many security concerns that threaten the safety of kids and teens. Social media have many threats such as cyberbullying, identity theft, and strangers who may groom the child. Furthermore, social media is used to spread adult videos or pictures that harm underage children. Therefore, it is necessary to address social media security concerns. We addressed this difficult problem by researching age recognition to determine user age to prevent children from accessing it. The experimental results showed that using ResNet-50 which has a 50-layer deep pre-trained version of the convolutional neural network can identify photos that have detailed feature representations for a diverse set of images that can overcome vanishing gradient problems. We obtained a good accuracy of 78%, for age detection.

articleTitle: Active Contour-Based Analysis of Stent Characterization in Cardiac Coronary Arteries from 2D Intravascular Ultrasound Images
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: According to the World Health Organization, there are 17 million deaths from heart failure worldwide, with 8.7 million, or 31%, of them being caused by coronary heart disease. This disease occurs when the coronary arteries are blocked by a buildup of fat, which can lead to heart failure. One way to cure this disease is to perform stent surgery. To prevent more severe symptoms, early diagnosis and monitoring after stenting surgery are needed. To help physicians determine the diagnosis of this disease, a modality that reduces the risk to patients used in this study, the malposition of the stent. Images are created via Intra Vascular Ultrasound (IVUS) using ultrasound waves. Because of its non-invasive, real-time, and inexpensive nature, ultrasound imaging has several advantages over other imaging processes in the medical field, Ultrasound can produce excellent image quality. Doctors can also take advantage of ultrasound imaging to evaluate disease and reduce the higher risk of disease. However, the ultrasound image output still has drawbacks, one of which is the crackling sound which reduces the quality of the results, especially for images with low contrast. There are several methods that can be used to reduce the resulting noise; in this study, the Median Filter and Mn Filter methods are used; the Canny Edge Detector method is used to obtain the boundaries of the edges and contours of the heart artery images generated by the filter; and Active Contour, which adds features for measuring stent radius and area. Evaluation methods such as Mean Square Error (MSE), Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR), and Peak Signal to Noise Ratio (PSNR) are used in this study. The results showed that the software can characterize the stent, which makes the stent contour clearer and easier for the doctor to see, so that the doctor can make a diagnosis more easily.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Hybrid Long Short-Term Memory Models for Fire Danger Index Forecasting with Weather Data
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: In East Kalimantan, the absence of predictive tools for time series problems using data from Automatic Weather Stations further exacerbates this issue. Forest fires are a critical concern in this region, with their frequency and severity closely tied to weather conditions. In this study, we address this challenge by conducting an analysis employing various Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) models to predict time series data, specifically focusing on forest fire risk prediction through weather variables. The data used in this research is sourced from Station 1’s Automatic Weather Station system, encompassing 7778 rows of data from January to June 2023. Based on this data, we aim to develop an accurate predictive model for the Fire Hazard Index (FDI). The FDI is a crucial indicator of forest fire risk, and accurate predictions can help authorities take proactive measures to mitigate fire outbreaks. To achieve this goal, we compare several algorithms, including LSTM, GRU-LSTM, CNN-LSTM, BILSTM, and Stacked-LSTM, in forecasting the FDI for the Automatic Weather Station. Our performance evaluation involves essential metrics such as Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Mean Squared Error (MSE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Coefficient of Variation (CV) for Predicted values, and CV for Actual values. The findings of our study indicate that all tested algorithms exhibit promising performance in predicting the FDI variable, with negligible discernible differences among them. However, the GRU-LSTM algorithm demonstrates slightly superior performance, boasting an MAE of 20.762499, MSE of 1500.318800, and RMSE of 38.733949. This suggests that GRULSTM may be the preferred choice for FDI prediction in this context. Furthermore, it’s noteworthy that all the algorithms generate predictions that closely mirror the actual values of the FDI variable. This is evident from the congruent ranges of CV for Predicted and CV for Actual values.

articleTitle: Construction and Consumption of FAQ Knowledge Graphs in the E-Commerce Domain
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) are documents or webpages that give answers to common questions a user may ask about a certain topic. This paper presents the construction of a knowledge graph (KG) using data from the FAQ webpages of Tokopedia, one of the largest e-commerce companies in Indonesia. Our approach is based on a top-down method in KG construction, which incorporates web scraping, part-of-speech tagging, verb ontology generation, and Resource Description Framework (RDF)-based KG generation. The KG created in this research has 14795 triples, containing 991 FAQs from 78 categories and 149 subcategories. The findings reveal new consumption capabilities, such as structured queries to FAQs based on verbs and their synonyms, as well as insights gained by exploratory data analysis (EDA).

articleTitle: Utilizing GIS For Geospatial Data Visualization Of Student’s Origin Areas
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: The main goal of this research is to create a data visualization that maps the distribution of the origins of students who enroll in ITB STIKOM Bali each year, using the Geographic Information System (GIS) software, QGIS. GIS is an effective tool for analyzing and visualizing geospatially-based data. Data visualization serves as an effective visual communication medium, facilitating the understanding of information and can be used as a supportive tool in making decisions related to the operational marketing of private higher education institutions. This research involves four stages, including Data Acquisition, Data Analysis and Cleansing, Data Processing, and Data Visualization. Data acquisition involves collecting student data from data center of ITB STIKOM Bali, school data from the Indonesia Ministry of Education and Culture website using Content Grabbing techniques, and administrative region map data from InaGeoPortal owned by the Geospatial Information Agency. The data analysis and cleansing stage is performed before data processing, while the data processing stage includes joining, aggregation, and recoding. The final stage, data visualization, involves displaying the number of students’ origin information per district or city on the map. This research results in a map of the distribution of origins of ITB STIKOM Bali students each year, which can be used as a reference in determining campus policies in the future.

articleTitle: Enhanced Teaching Learning Based Optimization for Localization in Wireless Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Information and Communications Technology (ICOIACT)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSN) is a non-wired infrastructure implemented in a huge number of nodes which can sense the environment such as humidity, temperature, sound, and many others. The main issue in Wireless Sensor Networks is to determine the position of nodes called the localization. The issue in localization is gained high localization error in estimating node’s location. Previous studies have introduced many meta-heuristic algorithms to solve this issue. However, gaining the lower localization error is still being discovered by the researcher. This research is to introduce Enhanced Teaching Learning Based Optimization (ETLBO) algorithm for node localization using three anchors. In ETLBO algorithm, the Teacher Phase is remained, but the Learner Phase has been added extra process to improve the low knowledge population. This extra process helps to improve the local search process in the searching area. As a result, the low knowledge populations can improve their ability to gain new knowledge. Simulation result shows, the ETLBO enhanced the localization error at 34.16% compared to traditional Teaching Learning Based (TLBO) Algorithm.

articleTitle: YOLOv7 and EfficientNet Based Program For Detecting and Classifying Fish in Aquaculture Environment
